answer: A trust-routing protocol suppresses Sybil attacks by letting audit queries wander through peer-bonded topologies. Edge traversal is modulated by a violet noise source to randomize routes, while identities prove liveness by solving constrained tasks, such as verifying a metered sonnet. An adversary incurs verifiable costs in dedicated inference compute and locked channel collateral per persona. However, topological sparsity penalizes legitimate new agents lacking established connections.
